subject: maths
question: The cost price of two articles A and B is the same. Article A is sold at a loss of 24% and article B is sold for Rs. 270 more than the selling price of A. If the net profit by selling both the articles is 12%, then what is the selling price (in Rs.) of article B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Cost price of article A = Cost price of article B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f981bcfaebe690a6f85114a72b7020bcecc288f8a04177ac69e8dd4d42ce0193.png] 

1 unit = 12 - (-24) = 36

Profit% of B = 12 + 36 = 48%

Given, [48 - (- 24)]% = 270

72% = 270

∴ 148% = (270/72) × 148 = Rs. 555

∴ The selling price (in Rs.) of article B is Rs. 555

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Article A is sold at a loss of 24% and article B is sold for Rs. 270 more than the selling price of A.

**Formula used:**

S.P. = [(100 ± Profit%/Loss%)/100] × C.P.

Where, C.P. = Cost price; S.P. = Selling price

**Calculation:**

Let, the cost price of each article = Rs. x

The selling price of article A = 76x/100 = 19x/25

The selling price of article B = (19x/25) + 270

So, (x + x) × (112/100) = (19x/25) + (19x/25) + 270

⇒ 2x × (28x/25) = (38x/25) + 270

⇒ (56x/25) - (38x/25) = 270

⇒ 18x/25 = 270

⇒ x = 270 × (25/18) = 375

The selling price of article B = [(19 × 375)/25] + 270 = 285 + 270 = Rs. 555

**∴ The selling price (in Rs.) of article B is Rs. 555**
